messages:
alyssa: quick heads up — I'm proposing a 'softbind' binding mode to replace and simplify some of our pin TTL semantics. want to align on telemetry and migration before I update the RFC.

mike: tl;dr?

alyssa: short version: softbind = best-effort affinity. runtime will prefer the pinned variant but can transparently fall back to a compatible model when capacity/compat issues arise. hardbind = strict: runtime returns an explicit failure (409) if requested variant isn't resolvable. goal: make softbind the default rollout semantics to reduce noisy rollouts and customer incidents.

jia: how do we avoid silent regressions if softbind falls back? we need ways to detect & alert when traffic is silently served by fallback models.

alyssa: agreed. propose three lightweight telemetry fields emitted per request: bind.outcome (preferred|compatible|fallback), bind.reason (capacity|compat|notfound), and bind.latency.delta (ms difference between preferred vs actual). Also emit a per-release confusion metric for eval/prompt-sets.

samir: multi-tenant concern: some customers require hard guarantees (compliance). there should be an opt-in per-rollout metadata flag to force hardbind. also need a migration plan for existing pinned leases.

anya: +1. enterprise customers should be able to opt into hardbind by default via tenant config. devex should document SDK behavior for both modes.

mike: routing questions — how does the router pick the fallback order? do we maintain weights or simple priority lists?

alyssa: plan is a hybrid: rollout metadata provides three ordered sets: preferred, compatible, fallback (ordered). router computes a softbind score and will pick first available model in those lists. if we add weights later, it'll be an optional field. example rollout metadata (draft):
```
{
  "binding": "soft",
  "preferred": ["my-model@v1.3.2"],
  "compatible": ["my-model@v1.2.x", "my-model-quant@v1.3.2-q4"],
  "fallback_policy": "ordered"
}
```

jia: we should also expose resolver headers so clients/SDKs can detect and log when fallback happens: e.g., X-Model-Resolved and X-Bind-Outcome. SDKs can surface a warning or increment a local metric.

samir: add these metrics to the ops playbook: bind_fallsback_total, bind_forced_409_total, and per-tenant bind_fallback_rate. that'll help SREs set alerts.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout my-model v1.3.2 -> v1.4.0 started (5% traffic), binding=soft.

anya: devex: I'll take a doc PR for SDK header handling and a sample migration guide for tenants moving from old pin TTLs to binding semantics.

alyssa: actionables I will take: update RFC with new field names (binding, preferred/compatible/fallback lists), telemetry spec (bind.outcome/reason/latency.delta), and migration notes (map old pinned leases -> binding: hard if TTL==infinite else binding: soft with remaining ttl). plan to ship opt-in softbind default for non-enterprise tenants in 2 weeks. objections?

mike: please include a short compatibility shim: if client specifies explicit model-id in header, honor hardbind semantics even if rollout binding is soft. add migration note for pinned leases -> binding field.

jia: +1 to telemetry and headers. also add a tiny eval harness to detect quality regressions when fallback happens.

alyssa: thanks — will update RFC and ping arch for final sign-off later today.
